en.name: Martin I
en.summary: The only pope venerated as a martyr for his death in Byzantine exile, arrested for defying the emperor's Monothelite decree.
en.body: Martin I convened the Lateran Council of 649 without imperial approval, formally condemning Monothelitism and the emperor Constans II's Typos decree that had sought to suppress debate on the issue. In retaliation, Byzantine forces seized Martin from Rome, transported him to Constantinople for a humiliating public trial, and exiled him to Crimea, where he died from the harsh conditions — making him the last pope to date venerated as a martyr.
